metadata.title: The primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions

nodes.name: Linear forms condition
nodes.statement:
Let $
u : \mathbb{Z}_N ightarrow \mathbb{R}^{+}$ be a measure. Let $m_0,t_0$ and $L_0$ be small positive integer parameters. Then we say that $
u$ satisfies the $(m_0,t_0,L_0)$-linear forms condition if the following holds. Let $m \leq m_0$ and $t \leq t_0$ be arbitrary, and suppose that $( L_{ij} )_{1 \leq i \leq m, 1 \leq j \leq t}$ are arbitrary rational numbers with numerator and denominator at most $L_0$ in absolute value, and that $b_i$, $1 \leq i \leq m$, are arbitrary elements of $\mathbb{Z}_N$.  For $1 \leq i \leq m$, let $\psi_i: \Z_N^t 	o \Z_N$ be the linear forms $\psi_i(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{j = 1}^t L_{ij}x_j + b_i$, where $\mathbf{x} = (x_1,\dots,x_t) \in \mathbb{Z}_N^t$, and where the rational numbers $L_{ij}$ are interpreted as elements of $\Z_N$ in the usual manner (assuming $N$ is prime and larger than $L_0$). Suppose that as $i$ ranges over $1,\ldots,m$, the $t$-tuples $(L_{ij})_{1 \leq j \leq t} \in \Q^t$ are non-zero, and no $t$-tuple is a rational multiple of any other. Then we have  egin{equation} \mathbb{E}\left( 
u(\psi_1(\mathbf{x})) \dots 
u(\psi_m(\mathbf{x})) \;|\; \mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{Z}_N^t ight) = 1 + o_{L_0,m_0,t_0}(1). \end{equation} Note that the rate of decay in the $o(1)$ term is assumed to be uniform in the choice of $b_1, \ldots, b_m$.

nodes.name: Correlation condition
nodes.statement:
Let $
u : \mathbb{Z}_N ightarrow \mathbb{R}^{+}$ be a measure, and let $m_0$ be a positive integer parameter. We say that $
u$ satisfies the $m_0$-correlation condition if for every $1 < m \leq m_0$ there exists a weight function $	au = 	au_{m}: \mathbb{Z}_N 	o \R^+$ which obeys the moment conditions  egin{equation} \E( 	au^q ) = O_{m,q}(1) \end{equation} for all $1 \leq q < \infty$ and such that  egin{equation} \E( 
u(x+h_1) 
u(x+h_2) \ldots 
u(x+h_m) \; |\;  x \in \mathbb{Z}_N) \leq \sum_{1 \leq i < j \leq m} 	au(h_i-h_j) \end{equation} for all $h_1, \ldots, h_m \in \Z_N$ (not necessarily distinct).

nodes.name: Pseudorandom measures ($k$-pseudorandom)
nodes.statement: Let $\nu : \mathbb{Z}_N \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{+}$ be a measure. We say that $\nu$ is $k$-pseudorandom if it satisfies the $(k\cdot 2^{k-1},3k - 4,k)$-linear forms condition and also the $2^{k-1}$-correlation condition.

nodes.name: $L^q$ norms and Hilbert space $L^2(\Z_N)$
nodes.statement: For every $1 \leq q \leq \infty$ and $f: \mathbb{Z}_N \to \R$, we define the $L^q$ norms as $$\|f\|_{L^q} := \E(|f|^q)^{1/q}$$ with the usual convention that $\|f\|_{L^\infty} := \sup_{x \in \mathbb{Z}_N} |f(x)|$.  We let $L^q(\Z_N)$ be the Banach space of all functions from $\Z_N$ to $\R$ equipped with the $L^q$ norm; of course since $\Z_N$ is finite these spaces are all equal to each other as vector spaces, but the norms are only equivalent up to powers of $N$.  We also observe that $L^2(\Z_N)$ is a real Hilbert space with the usual inner product $$ \langle f, g \rangle := \E( f g ).$$ If $\Omega$ is a subset of $\mathbb{Z}_N$, we use ${\bf 1}_\Omega: \mathbb{Z}_N \to \R$ to denote the indicator function of $\Omega$, thus ${\bf 1}_\Omega(x) = 1$ if $x \in \Omega$ and ${\bf 1}_\Omega(x) = 0$ otherwise.  Similarly if $P(x)$ is a statement concerning an element $x \in \Z_N$, we write ${\bf 1}_{P(x)}$ for ${\bf 1}_{\{ x \in \Z_N: P(x) \}}(x)$.

nodes.name: $d$-dimensional Gowers inner product
nodes.section: Gowers uniformity norms, and a generalized von Neumann theorem
nodes.statement: Let $d \geq 0$ be a dimension. We let $\{0,1\}^d$ be the standard discrete $d$-dimensional cube, consisting of $d$-tuples $\omega = (\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_d)$ where $\omega_j \in \{0,1\}$ for $j=1,\ldots,d$. If $h = (h_1,\ldots,h_d) \in \mathbb{Z}_N^d$ we define $\omega \cdot h := \omega_1 h_1 + \ldots + \omega_d h_d$.  If $(f_\omega)_{\omega \in \{0,1\}^d}$ is a $\{0,1\}^d$-tuple of functions in $L^\infty(\mathbb{Z}_N)$, we define the \emph{$d$-dimensional Gowers inner product} $\langle (f_\omega)_{\omega \in \{0,1\}^d} \rangle_{U^d}$ by the formula \begin{equation} \langle (f_\omega)_{\omega \in \{0,1\}^d} \rangle_{U^d} := \E\bigg( \prod_{\omega \in \{0,1\}^d} f_\omega(x + \omega \cdot h) \; \bigg| \; x \in \mathbb{Z}_N, h \in \mathbb{Z}_N^d \bigg). \end{equation}

nodes.name: $\sigma$-algebra, atoms, and conditional expectation
nodes.statement: A \emph{$\sigma$-algebra} $\B$ in $\mathbb{Z}_N$ is any collection of subsets of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ which contains the empty set $\emptyset$ and the full set $\Z_N$, and is closed under complementation, unions and intersections.  As $\mathbb{Z}_N$ is a finite set, we will not need to distinguish between countable and uncountable unions or intersections.  We define the \emph{atoms} of a $\sigma$-algebra to be the minimal non-empty elements of $\B$ (with respect to set inclusion); it is clear that the atoms in $\B$ form a partition of $\mathbb{Z}_N$, and $\B$ consists precisely of arbitrary unions of its atoms (including the empty union $\emptyset$). A function $f \in L^q(\mathbb{Z}_N)$ is said to be \emph{measurable} with respect to a $\sigma$-algebra $\B$ if all the level sets $\{f^{-1}(\{x\}): x \in \R \}$ of $f$ lie in $\B$, or equivalently if $f$ is constant on each of the atoms of $\B$. We define $L^q(\B) \subseteq L^q(\mathbb{Z}_N)$ to be the subspace of $L^q(\mathbb{Z}_N)$ consisting of $\B$-measurable functions, equipped with the same $L^q$ norm.  We can then define the conditional expectation operator $f \mapsto \E(f|\B)$ to be the orthogonal projection of $L^2(\mathbb{Z}_N)$ to $L^2(\B)$; this is of course also defined on all the other $L^q(\mathbb{Z}_N)$ spaces since they are all the same vector space.  An equivalent definition of conditional expectation is $$ \E(f|\B)(x) := \E( f(y) | y \in \B(x) )$$ for all $x \in \mathbb{Z}_N$, where $\B(x)$ is the unique atom in $\B$ which contains $x$.  It is clear that conditional expectation is a linear self-adjoint orthogonal projection on $L^2(\mathbb{Z}_N)$, is a contraction on $L^q(\mathbb{Z}_N)$ for every $1 \leq q \leq \infty$, preserves non-negativity, and also preserves constant functions.  Also, if $\B'$ is a subalgebra of $\B$ then $\E(\E(f|\B) | \B') = \E(f|\B')$. If $\B_1, \ldots, \B_K$ are $\sigma$-algebras, we use $\bigvee_{j=1}^K \B_j = \B_1 \vee \ldots \vee \B_K$ to denote the $\sigma$-algebra generated by these algebras, or in other words the algebra whose atoms are the intersections of atoms in $\B_1, \ldots, \B_K$.  We adopt the usual convention that when $K=0$, the join $\bigvee_{j=1}^K \B_j$ is just the trivial $\sigma$-algebra $\{ \emptyset, \Z_N\}$.

nodes.name: Goldston--Y{\i}ld{\i}r{\i}m truncated divisor sum $\Lambda_R$
nodes.section: A pseudorandom measure which majorises the primes
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a parameter (in applications it will be a small power of $N$). Define \[ \Lambda_R(n) := \sum_{\substack{d | n \\ d \leq R}} \mu(d)\log (R/d) = \sum_{d|n} \mu(d) \log(R/d)_+.\]

nodes.name: The majorant measure $\nu$
nodes.section: A pseudorandom measure which majorises the primes
nodes.statement: Let $R := N^{k^{-1}2^{-k-4}}$, and let $\epsilon_k := 1/2^{k}(k+4)!$.  We define the function $\nu: \Z_N \to \R^+$ by \[ \nu(n) \; := \; \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} \frac{\phi(W)}{W} \frac{\Lambda_R(Wn + 1)^2}{\log R} & \hbox{ when } \epsilon_k N \leq n \leq 2\epsilon_k N\\ 1 & \hbox{ otherwise} \end{array}\right. \] for all $0 \leq n < N$, where we identify $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ with $\Z_N$ in the usual manner.

nodes.name: Domain $\D^m_\sigma$ and $C^k(\D^m_\sigma)$ norm
nodes.statement: For any $\sigma > 0$, let $\D^m_\sigma \subseteq\C^{2m}$ denote the domain \[ \D^m_\sigma := \{z_j,z'_j : -\sigma < \Re(z_j),\Re(z'_j) < 100, j = 1,\dots,m\}.\] If $G = G(z,z')$ is an analytic function of $2m$ complex variables on $\D^m_\sigma$, we define the $C^k(\D^m_\sigma)$ norm of $G$ for any integer $k \geq 0$ as $$ \| G \|_{C^k(\D^m_\sigma)} := \sup_{a_1,\dots,a_m,a'_1,\dots,a'_m} \big\Vert \big(\frac{\partial}{\partial z_1}\big)^{a_1} \ldots \big(\frac{\partial}{\partial z_m}\big)^{a_m} \big(\frac{\partial}{\partial z'_1}\big)^{a'_1} \ldots \big(\frac{\partial}{\partial z'_m}\big)^{a'_m} G \big\Vert_{L^\infty(\D^m_\sigma)}$$ where $a_1,\ldots,a_m,a'_1,\dots,a'_m$ range over all non-negative integers with total sum at most $k$.

nodes.name: Uniform cover
nodes.statement: Suppose that $A$ and $B$ are finite non-empty sets and that $\Phi: A \to B$ is a map. Then we say that $\Phi$ is a \textit{uniform cover of $B$ by $A$} if $\Phi$ is surjective and all the fibers $\{ \Phi^{-1}(b): b \in B\}$ have the same cardinality (i.e. they have cardinality $|A|/|B|$).  Observe that if $\Phi$ is a uniform cover of $B$ by $A$, then for any function $f: B \to \R$ we have \begin{equation} \E( f(\Phi(a)) | a \in A ) = \E( f(b) | b \in B ). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Dual function $\mathcal{D}F$
nodes.statement: For each function $F \in L^1(\Z_N)$, define the \emph{dual function} ${\mathcal D} F$ of $F$ by \begin{equation} {\mathcal D} F(x) := \E\bigg( \prod_{\omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}: \omega \neq 0^{k-1}} F(x + \omega \cdot h) \; \bigg| \; h \in \mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1} \bigg) \end{equation} where $0^{k-1}$ denotes the element of $\{0,1\}^{k-1}$ consisting entirely of zeroes.

nodes.name: Gowers anti-uniform function
nodes.statement: We say that $g$ is \emph{Gowers anti-uniform} if $\|g\|_{(U^{k-1})^*} = O(1)$ and $\|g\|_{L^\infty} = O(1)$. If $g$ is Gowers anti-uniform, and if $|\langle f,g \rangle|$ is large, then $f$ cannot be Gowers uniform (have small Gowers norm) since \[ |\langle f,g \rangle| \leq \Vert f \Vert_{U^{k-1}}\Vert g \Vert_{(U^{k-1})^*}.\] Thus Gowers anti-uniform functions can be thought of as ``obstructions to Gowers uniformity''.

nodes.name: Modified von Mangoldt function $\widetilde{\Lambda}$ ($W$-trick)
nodes.section: A pseudorandom measure which majorises the primes
nodes.statement: Let $\w = \w(N)$ be any function tending slowly to infinity with $N$, so that $1/\w(N) = o(1)$, and let $W = \prod_{p \leq \w(N)} p$ be the product of the primes up to $\w(N)$. Define the modified von Mangoldt function $\tilde \Lambda: \Z^+ \to \R^+$ by \[ \widetilde{\Lambda}(n) := \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} \frac{\phi(W)}{W} \log(Wn + 1) & \hbox{ when } Wn+1 \hbox{ is prime}\\ 0 & \hbox{ otherwise.} \end{array}\right.\]

nodes.name: Main theorem (primes contain long APs)
nodes.statement: The prime numbers contain infinitely many arithmetic progressions of length $k$ for all $k$.
conclusions: The prime numbers contain infinitely many arithmetic progressions of length $k$ for all $k$.

nodes.name: Szemer\'edi's theorem in the primes
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be any subset of the prime numbers of positive relative upper density, thus $\limsup_{N \to \infty} \pi(N)^{-1}|A \cap [1,N]| > 0$, where $\pi(N)$ denotes the number of primes less than or equal to $N$.  Then $A$ contains infinitely many arithmetic progressions of length $k$ for all $k$.
assumptions: Let $A$ be any subset of the prime numbers of positive relative upper density, thus $\limsup_{N \to \infty} \pi(N)^{-1}|A \cap [1,N]| > 0$, where $\pi(N)$ denotes the number of primes less than or equal to $N$.
conclusions: $A$ contains infinitely many arithmetic progressions of length $k$ for all $k$.

nodes.name: Szemer\'edi's theorem relative to a pseudorandom measure
nodes.statement: Let $k \geq 3$ and $0 < \delta \leq 1$  be fixed parameters. Suppose that $\nu: \mathbb{Z}_N \to \R^+$ is $k$-pseudorandom. Let $f: \mathbb{Z}_N \to \R^+$ be any non-negative function obeying the bound \begin{equation} 0 \leq f(x) \leq \nu(x) \hbox{ for all } x \in \mathbb{Z}_N \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \E(f) \geq \delta. \end{equation} Then we have \begin{equation} \E( f(x) f(x+r) \ldots f(x+(k-1)r) | x,r \in \mathbb{Z}_N ) \geq c(k,\delta) - o_{k,\delta}(1) \end{equation} where $c(k,\delta) > 0$ is the same constant which appears in Proposition \ref{sz}.  \textup{(}The decay rate $o_{k,\delta}(1)$, on the other hand, decays significantly slower than that in Proposition \ref{sz}, and depends of course on the decay rates in the linear forms and correlation conditions\textup{)}.
assumptions: Let $f: \mathbb{Z}_N \to \R^+$ be any non-negative function obeying the bound $0 \leq f(x) \leq \nu(x)$ for all $x \in \mathbb{Z}_N$
conclusions: $\E( f(x) f(x+r) \ldots f(x+(k-1)r) | x,r \in \mathbb{Z}_N ) \geq c(k,\delta) - o_{k,\delta}(1)$ where $c(k,\delta) > 0$ is the same constant which appears in Proposition \ref{sz}.

nodes.name: Erd\H{o}s conjecture on arithmetic progressions
nodes.statement: Suppose that $A = \{a_1 < a_2 < \dots\}$ is an infinite sequence of integers such that $\sum 1/a_i = \infty$. Then $A$ contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions.

nodes.name: Szemer\'edi's theorem (finitary version)
nodes.statement: Let $N$ be a positive integer and let $\mathbb{Z}_N := \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$. Let $\delta > 0$ be a fixed positive real number, and let $k \geq 3$ be an integer. Then there is a minimal $N_0(\delta,k) < \infty$ with the following property. If $N \geq N_0(\delta,k)$ and $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_N$ is any set of cardinality at least $\delta N$, then $A$ contains an arithmetic progression of length $k$.

nodes.name: Szemer\'edi's theorem, again
nodes.statement: Write $\vconstlem : \mathbb{Z}_N \rightarrow \R^+$ for the constant function $\vconstlem \equiv 1$. Let $0 < \delta \leq 1$ and $k \geq 1$ be fixed.  Let $N$ be a large integer parameter, and let $f: \mathbb{Z}_N \to \R^+$ be a non-negative function obeying the bounds \begin{equation} 0 \leq f(x) \leq \vconstlem(x) \hbox{ for all } x \in \mathbb{Z}_N \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \E(f(x) | x \in \mathbb{Z}_N) \geq \delta.\end{equation} Then we have $$ \E( f(x) f(x+r) \ldots f(x+(k-1)r) | x,r \in \mathbb{Z}_N) \geq c(k,\delta) - o_{k,\delta}(1)$$ for some constant $c(k,\delta) > 0$ which does not depend on $f$ or $N$.

nodes.name: Generalised von Neumann
nodes.section: Gowers uniformity norms, and a generalized von Neumann theorem
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $
u$ is $k$-pseudorandom. Let $f_0, \ldots, f_{k-1} \in L^1(\Z_N)$ be functions which are pointwise bounded by $
u+\vconstlem$, or in other words  egin{equation} |f_j(x)| \leq 
u(x) + 1 \hbox{ for all } x \in \mathbb{Z}_N, 0 \leq j \leq k-1. \end{equation} Let $c_0, \ldots, c_{k-1}$ be a permutation of some $k$ consecutive elements of $\{-k+1,\dots,-1,0,1,\ldots,k-1\}$ 	extup{(}in practice we will take $c_j := j$	extup{)}. Then \[ \E igg( \prod_{j=0}^{k-1} f_j(x + c_j r) \;   igg| \; x,r \in \mathbb{Z}_N  igg) = O ig(\inf_{0 \leq j \leq k-1} \| f_j \|_{U^{k-1}} ig) + o(1).\]

nodes.name: Uniform distribution wrt basic Gowers anti-uniform functions
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\nu$ is $k$-pseudorandom. Let $K \geq 1$ be a fixed integer, let $\Phi: I^K \to \R$ be a fixed continuous function, let $\D F_1, \ldots, \D F_K$ be basic Gowers anti-uniform functions, and define the function $\psi: \Z_N \to \R$ by \[ \psi(x) := \Phi({\mathcal D} F_1(x), \ldots, {\mathcal D} F_K(x)).\] Then we have the estimate $$ \langle \nu - 1, \psi \rangle = o_{K,\Phi}(1).$$ Furthermore if $\Phi$ ranges over a compact set $E \subset C^0(I^K)$ of the space $C^0(I^K)$ of continuous functions on $I^K$ \textup{(}in the uniform topology\textup{)} then the bounds here are uniform in $\Phi$ \textup{(}i.e. one can replace $o_{K,\Phi}(1)$ with $o_{K,E}(1)$ in this case\textup{)}.

nodes.name: Each function generates a $\sigma$-algebra
nodes.statement:
Let $
u$ be a $k$-pseudorandom measure, let $0 < \eps < 1$ and $0 < \eta < 1/2$ be parameters, and let $G \in L^\infty(\Z_N)$ be function taking values in the interval $I := [-2^{2^{k-1}}, 2^{2^{k-1}} ]$. Then there exists a $\sigma$-algebra $\B_{\eps,\eta}(G)$ with the following properties:  egin{itemize} \item 	extup{($G$ lies in its own $\sigma$-algebra)} For any $\sigma$-algebra $\B$, we have  egin{equation} \| G - \E( G | \B \vee \B_{\eps,\eta}(G)) \|_{L^\infty(\Z_N)} \leq \eps. \end{equation} \item 	extup{(Bounded complexity)} $\B_{\eps,\eta}(G)$ is generated by at most $O(1/\eps)$ atoms. \item 	extup{(Approximation by continuous functions of $G$)}  If $A$ is any atom in $\B_{\eps,\eta}(G)$, then there exists a continuous function $\Psi_A: I 	o [0,1]$ such that  egin{equation} \| ({ f 1}_A - \Psi_A(G))(
u + 1) \|_{L^1(\Z_N)} = O(\eta). \end{equation} Furthermore, $\Psi_A$ lies in a fixed compact set $E = E_{\eps,\eta}$ of $C^0(I)$ 	extup{(}which is independent of $F$, $
u$, $N$, or $A$	extup{)}. \end{itemize}

nodes.name: $\sigma$-algebra generated by basic Gowers anti-uniform functions
nodes.statement:
Let $
u$ be a $k$-pseudorandom measure.  Let $K \geq 1$ be an fixed integer and let $\D F_1, \ldots, \D F_K \in L^{\infty}(\Z_N)$ be basic Gowers anti-uniform functions.  Let $0 < \eps < 1$ and $0 < \eta < 1/2$ be parameters, and let $\B_{\eps,\eta}(\D F_j)$, $j=1,\ldots,K$, be constructed as in Proposition ef{sigma-gen}.  Let $\B := \B_{\eps,\eta}(\D F_1) \vee \ldots \vee \B_{\eps,\eta}(\D F_K)$.  Then if $\eta < \eta_0(\epsilon, K)$ is sufficiently small and $N > N_0(\epsilon, K, \eta)$ is sufficiently large we have  egin{equation} \| \D F_j - \E( \D F_j | \B) \|_{L^\infty(\Z_N)} \leq \eps \hbox{ for all } 1 \leq j \leq K. \end{equation} Furthermore there exists a set $\Omega$ which lies in $\B$ such that  egin{equation} \E( (
u + 1) { f 1}_{\Omega} ) = O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}) \end{equation} and such that  egin{equation} \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega}) \E(
u - 1 | \B) \|_{L^\infty(\Z_N)} = O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Generalised Koopman-von Neumann structure theorem
nodes.section: A Furstenberg tower, and the proof of Theorem \ref{main}
nodes.statement:
Let $
u$ be a $k$-pseudorandom measure, and let $f \in L^1(\Z_N)$ be a non-negative function satisfying $0 \leq f(x) \leq 
u(x)$ for all $x \in \Z_N$. Let $0 < \eps \ll 1$ be a small parameter, and assume $N > N_0(\eps)$ is sufficiently large. Then there exists a $\sigma$-algebra $\B$ and an exceptional set $\Omega \in \B$ such that  egin{itemize} \item 	extup{(}smallness condition	extup{)}  egin{equation} \E( 
u { f 1}_{\Omega} ) = o_\eps(1); \end{equation} \item 	extup{(}$
u$ is uniformly distributed outside of $\Omega$	extup{)}  egin{equation} \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega}) \E( 
u - 1 | \B) \|_{L^\infty} = o_{\eps}(1) \end{equation} and \item 	extup{(}Gowers uniformity estimate	extup{)}  egin{equation} \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega}) (f - \E(f|\B)) \|_{U^{k-1}} \leq \eps^{1/2^k}. \end{equation} \end{itemize}

nodes.name: Iterative Step
nodes.section: A Furstenberg tower, and the proof of Theorem \ref{main}
nodes.statement:
Let $
u$ be a $k$-pseudorandom measure, and let $f \in L^1(\Z_N)$ be a non-negative function satisfying $0 \leq f(x) \leq 
u(x)$ for all $x \in \Z_N$. Let $0 <\eta \ll \eps \ll 1$ be small numbers, and let $K \geq 0$ be an integer.  Suppose that $\eta < \eta_0(\eps, K)$ is sufficiently small and that $N > N_0(\eps, K,\eta)$ is sufficiently large. Let $F_1,\ldots,F_K \in L^1(\Z_N)$ be a collection of functions obeying the pointwise bounds  egin{equation} |F_{j}(x)| \leq (1 + O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2})) (
u(x) + 1) \end{equation} for all $1 \leq j \leq K$ and $x \in \Z_N$.  Let $\B_K$ be the $\sigma$-algebra  egin{equation} \B_K :=  \B_{\eps,\eta}(\D F_1) \vee \ldots \vee \B_{\eps,\eta}(\D F_K) \end{equation} where $\B_{\eps,\eta}(\D F_j)$ is as in Proposition ef{sigma-gen}, and suppose that there exists a set $\Omega_K$ in $\Z_N$ obeying  egin{itemize} \item 	extup{(}smallness bound	extup{)}  egin{equation} \E( (
u + 1) { f 1}_{\Omega_K} ) = O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}) \end{equation} and \item 	extup{(}uniform distribution bound	extup{)}  egin{equation} \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K}}) \E( 
u - 1 | \B_{K} )\|_{L^\infty(\Z_N)} = O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}). \end{equation} \end{itemize} Set  egin{equation} F_{K+1} := (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_K}) (f - \E(f|\B_K)) \end{equation} and suppose that $F_{K+1}$ obeys the non-Gowers-uniformity estimate  egin{equation} \| F_{K+1} \|_{U^{k-1}} > \eps^{1/2^k}. \end{equation} Then we have the estimates  egin{equation} \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_K}) \E(f|\B_K) \|_{L^\infty(\Z_N)} \leq 1 + O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}) \end{equation} 	extup{(}$\E (f | \B_K)$ is bounded outside $\Omega_K$	extup{)} and  egin{equation} |F_{K+1}(x)| \leq (1 + O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2})) (
u(x) + 1). \end{equation} Furthermore, if we let $\B_{K+1}$ be the $\sigma$-algebra  egin{equation} \B_{K+1} := \B_K \vee \B_{\eps,\eta}(\D F_{K+1}) = \B_{\eps,\eta}(\D F_1) \vee \ldots \vee \B_{\eps,\eta}(\D F_{K+1}) \end{equation} then there exists a set $\Omega_{K+1} \supseteq \Omega_K$ obeying  egin{itemize} \item 	extup{(}smallness bound	extup{)}  egin{equation} \E( (
u + 1) { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}} ) = O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}); \end{equation} \item 	extup{(}uniform distribution bound	extup{)}  egin{equation} \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) \E( 
u - 1 | \B_{K+1} )\|_{L^\infty(\Z_N)} = O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}). \end{equation} and such that we have \item 	extup{(}energy increment property	extup{)}  egin{equation} \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) \E(f|\B_{K+1}) \|_{L^2(\Z_N)}^2 \geq \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_K}) \E(f|\B_K) \|_{L^2(\Z_N)}^2 + 2^{-2^k + 1} \eps. \end{equation} \end{itemize}

nodes.name: Pseudorandom majorant for the primes
nodes.section: A pseudorandom measure which majorises the primes
nodes.statement: Write $\epsilon_k := 1/2^{k}(k+4)!$, and let $N$ be a sufficiently large prime number.  Then there is a $k$-pseudorandom measure $\nu : \mathbb{Z}_N \rightarrow \R^+$ such that $\nu(n) \geq k^{-1}2^{-k-5}\widetilde{\Lambda}(n)$ for all $\epsilon_k N \leq n \leq 2 \epsilon_k N$.

nodes.name: Goldston-Y{\i}ld{\i}r{\i}m (linear forms asymptotic for $\Lambda_R$)
nodes.section: A pseudorandom measure which majorises the primes
nodes.statement: Let $m, t$ be positive integers.  For each $1 \leq i \leq m$, let $\psi_i(\mathbf{x}) := \sum_{j=1}^t L_{ij} x_j + b_i$, be linear forms with integer coefficients $L_{ij}$ such that $|L_{ij}| \leq \sqrt{\w(N)}/2$ for all $i = 1,\ldots m$ and $j=1,\ldots,t$. We assume that the $t$-tuples $(L_{ij})_{j=1}^t$ are never identically zero, and that no two $t$-tuples are rational multiples of each other. Write $\theta_i := W\psi_i + 1$.  Suppose that $B$ is a product $\prod_{i = 1}^t I_i \subset \R^t$ of $t$ intervals $I_i$, each of which having length  at least $R^{10m}$. Then \textup{(}if the function $\w(N)$ is sufficiently slowly growing in $N$\textup{)} \[ \E( \Lambda_R(\theta_1(\mathbf{x}))^2 \dots \Lambda_R(\theta_m(\mathbf{x}))^2 | \x \in B ) = (1 + o_{m,t}(1)) \left(\frac{W \log R}{\phi(W)}\right)^m. \]

nodes.name: Goldston-Y{\i}ld{\i}r{\i}m (higher order correlations for $\Lambda_R$)
nodes.section: A pseudorandom measure which majorises the primes
nodes.statement: Let $m \geq 1$ be an integer, and let $B$ be an interval of length  at least $R^{10m}$. Suppose that $h_1,\dots,h_m$ are distinct integers satisfying $|h_i| \leq N^2$ for all $1 \leq i \leq m$, and let $\Delta$ denote the integer \[ \Delta := \prod_{1 \leq i < j \leq m} |h_i - h_j|.\] Then (for $N$ sufficiently large depending on $m$, and assuming the function $\w(N)$ sufficiently slowly growing in $N$) \begin{equation} \begin{split} \E( &\Lambda_R(W(x + h_1) + 1)^2 \dots \Lambda_R(W(x + h_m) + 1)^2| x \in B ) \\ &\leq (1 + o_m(1)) \left( \frac{W\log R}{\phi(W)}\right)^m \prod_{p | \Delta}(1 + O_m(p^{-1/2})). \end{split} \end{equation} Here and in the sequel, $p$ is always understood to be prime.

nodes.name: $\nu$ satisfies the linear forms condition
nodes.section: A pseudorandom measure which majorises the primes
nodes.statement: The function $\nu$ satisfies the $(k \cdot 2^{k-1},3k-4,k)$-linear forms condition.

nodes.name: $\nu$ satisfies the correlation condition
nodes.section: A pseudorandom measure which majorises the primes
nodes.statement: The measure $\nu$ satisfies the $2^{k-1}$-correlation condition.

nodes.name: Pseudorandom measures are star-shaped ($\nu_{1/2}$)
nodes.statement:
Let $
u$ be a $k$-pseudorandom measure.  Then $
u_{1/2} := (
u + \vconstlem)/2 = (
u + 1)/2$ is also a $k$-pseudorandom measure 	extup{(}though possibly with slightly different bounds in the $O()$ and $o()$ terms	extup{)}.

nodes.name: $\nu$ is close to $1$ in $U^d$
nodes.section: Gowers uniformity norms, and a generalized von Neumann theorem
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $
u$ is $k$-pseudorandom 	extup{(}as defined in Definition ef{mu-pseudo-def}	extup{)}. Then we have  egin{equation} \| 
u - \vconstlem \|_{U^d} = \| 
u - 1 \|_{U^d} = o(1) \end{equation} for all $1 \leq d \leq k-1$.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz (weighted cubes)
nodes.section: Gowers uniformity norms, and a generalized von Neumann theorem

nodes.name: $\nu$ covers its own cubes uniformly
nodes.section: Gowers uniformity norms, and a generalized von Neumann theorem
nodes.statement: For $n=0,2$, we have \[\E\bigg( |W(x,h)-1|^n \prod_{\omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}} \nu(x + \omega \cdot h)\; \bigg| \; x \in \mathbb{Z}_N, h \in \mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1} \bigg) = 0^n + o(1).\]

nodes.name: Lack of Gowers uniformity implies correlation
nodes.statement: Let $\nu$ be a $k$-pseudorandom measure, and let $F \in L^1(\Z_N)$ be any function.  Then we have the identities \begin{equation} \langle F, {\mathcal D} F \rangle = \| F \|_{U^{k-1}}^{2^{k-1}} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \| {\mathcal D} F \|_{(U^{k-1})^*} = \| F \|_{U^{k-1}}^{2^{k-1}-1}. \end{equation} If furthermore we assume the bounds \[ |F(x)| \leq \nu(x) + 1 \hbox{ for all } x \in \mathbb{Z}_N\] then we have the estimate \begin{equation} \| {\mathcal D} F \|_{L^\infty} \leq 2^{2^{k-1}-1} + o(1). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Polynomials of dual functions are Gowers anti-uniform
nodes.statement: Let $d \geq 1$.  For any polynomial $P$ of $K$ variables and degree $d$ with real coefficients \textup{(}independent of $N$\textup{)}, we have \[ \| P({\mathcal D} F_1, \ldots, {\mathcal D} F_K) \|_{(U^{k-1})^*} = O_{K,d,P}(1).\]

nodes.name: $\nu$ majorises $\widetilde{\Lambda}$
nodes.section: A pseudorandom measure which majorises the primes
nodes.statement: $\nu(n) \geq 0$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}_N$, and furthermore we have $\nu(n) \geq k^{-1}2^{-k-5}\widetilde{\Lambda}(n)$ for all $\epsilon_k N \leq n \leq 2\epsilon_kN$ \emph{(}if $N$ is sufficiently large depending on $k$\emph{)}.

nodes.name: $\nu$ is a measure ($\E(\nu)=1+o(1)$)
nodes.section: A pseudorandom measure which majorises the primes
nodes.statement: The measure $\nu$ constructed in Definition \ref{mu-def} obeys the estimate $\mathbb{E}(\nu) = 1 + o(1)$.

nodes.name: Additive weight function bound
nodes.section: A pseudorandom measure which majorises the primes
nodes.statement: Let $m \geq 1$ be a parameter. There is a weight function $\tau = \tau_m: \Z \to \R^+$ such that $\tau(n) \geq 1$ for all $n \neq 0$, and such that for all distinct $h_1,\ldots,h_j \in [\epsilon_k N, 2\epsilon_k N]$ we have \[ \prod_{p | \Delta}(1 + O_m(p^{-1/2})) \leq \sum_{1 \leq i < j \leq m} \tau(h_i - h_j),\] where $\Delta$ is defined in Proposition \ref{GY2}, and such that $\E( \tau^q(n) | 0 < |n| \leq N ) = O_{m,q}(1)$ for all $0< q < \infty$.

nodes.name: Local factor estimate
nodes.statement: If $p \leq \w(N)$, then $\omega_X(p) = 0$ for all non-empty $X$; in particular, $E_p = 1$ when $p \leq \w(N)$.  If instead $p > \w(N)$, then $\omega_X(p) = p^{-1}$ when $|X|=1$ and $\omega_X(p) \leq p^{-2}$ when $|X| \geq 2$.

nodes.name: Analytic continuation and estimates for $G_1,G_2$
nodes.statement: The Euler products $\prod_p E_p^{(j)}$ for $j=1,2$ are absolutely convergent in the domain $\D^m_{1/6m}$.  In particular, $G_1$, $G_2$ can be continued analytically to this domain.  Furthermore, we have the estimates \begin{align*} \| G_1 \|_{C^m(\D^m_{1/6m})} &\leq O_m(1) \\ \| G_2 \|_{C^m(\D^m_{1/6m})} &\leq O_{m,\w(N)}(1) \\ G_1(0,0) &= 1 + o_m(1) \\ G_2(0,0) &= (W/\phi(W))^m. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Contour integral estimate (zeta-bound)
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a positive real number. Let $G = G(z,z')$ be an analytic function of $2m$ complex variables on the domain $\D^m_\sigma$ for some $\sigma > 0$, and suppose that \begin{equation}\|G\|_{C^m(\D^m_\sigma)} = \exp(O_{m,\sigma}(\log^{1/3} R)).\end{equation} Then \[ \frac{1}{(2\pi i)^{2m}}\int_{\Gamma_1} \dots \int_{\Gamma_1} G(z,z')\prod_{j=1}^m \frac{\zeta(1+z_j + z'_j)}{\zeta(1 + z_j)\zeta(1 + z'_j)} \frac{R^{z_j + z'_j}}{z_j^2z^{\prime 2}_j} \, dz_jdz'_j  \] \[ = G(0,\dots,0) \log^m R + \sum_{j=1}^m O_{m,\sigma}(\| G \|_{C^j(\D^m_\sigma)} \log^{m-j} R) + O_{m,\sigma}(e^{-\delta \sqrt{\log R}})\] for some $\delta = \delta(m) > 0$.

nodes.name: Local factor estimate ($\omega_X(p)$, equal forms case)
nodes.statement: If $p \leq \w(N)$, then $\omega_X(p) = 0$ for all non-empty $X$; in particular, $E_p = 1$ when $p \leq \w(N)$.  If instead $p > \w(N)$, then $\omega_X(p) = p^{-1}$ when $|X|=1$ and $\omega_X(p) \leq p^{-1}$ when $|X| \geq 2$. Furthermore, if $|X| \geq 2$ then $\omega_X(p) = 0$ unless $p$ divides $\Delta := \prod_{1 \leq i < j \leq s} |h_i-h_j|$.

nodes.name: Analytic continuation and estimates for $G_0,G_1,G_2$
nodes.statement:
Let $0 < \sigma < 1/6m$.  Then the Euler products $\prod_p E_p^{(l)}$ for $l=0,1,2$ are absolutely convergent in the domain $\D^m_{\sigma}$.  In particular, $G_0$, $G_1$, $G_2$ can be continued analytically to this domain.  Furthermore, we have the estimates  egin{align} \| G_0 \|_{C^r(\D^m_{\sigma})} &\leq O_m \left(  rac{\log R}{\log \log R} ight)^r \prod_{p | \Delta} (1 + O_m(p^{2m\sigma-1})) \quad \hbox{ for } 0 \leq r \leq m \ \| G_0 \|_{C^m(\D^m_{1/6m})} &\leq \exp(O_m(\log^{1/3} R)) \ \| G_1 \|_{C^m(\D^m_{1/6m})} &\leq O_m(1) 
onumber\ \| G_2 \|_{C^m(\D^m_{1/6m})} &\leq O_{m,\w(N)}(1) 
onumber\ G_0(0,0) &= \prod_{p | \Delta} (1 + O_m(p^{-1/2}) ) \ G_1(0,0) &= 1 + o_m(1) 
onumber\ G_2(0,0) &= (W/\phi(W))^m.
onumber \end{align}

nodes.name: Zero-free region
nodes.statement: Define the \emph{classical zero free region} $\mathcal{Z}$ to be the closed region \[ \mathcal{Z} := \{ s \in \C: 10 \geq \Re s \geq 1 - \frac{\beta}{\log(|\Im s| + 2)} \}\] for some small $0 < \beta < 1$.  Then if $\beta$ is sufficiently small, $\zeta$ is non-zero and meromorphic in $\mathcal{Z}$ with a simple pole at 1 and no other singularities. Furthermore we have the bounds $$\zeta(s) - \frac{1}{s-1} = O(\log(|\Im s| + 2)); \quad \frac{1}{\zeta(s)} = O(\log(|\Im s| + 2))$$ for all $s \in \mathcal{Z}$.

nodes.name: Elementary integral estimates on contours
nodes.statement: Let $A,B$ be fixed constants with $A > 1$. Then we have the bounds. \begin{align} \int_{\Gamma_0} \log^B(|z| + 2)\left| \frac{R^zdz}{z^A}\right| &\leq O_{A,B}(e^{-\delta \sqrt{\log R}}); \\ \int_{\Gamma_1} \log^B(|z| + 2)\left| \frac{R^zdz}{z^2}\right| &\leq O_B(\log R). \end{align} Here $\delta = \delta(A,B,\beta) > 0$ is a constant independent of $R$.

nodes.name: Two-variable contour integral estimate ($m=1$ case)
nodes.statement: Let $f(z,z')$ be analytic in $\mathcal{D}_{\sigma}^1$ and suppose that \[|f(z,z')| \leq \exp(O_m(\log^{1/3}R))\] uniformly in this domain. Then the integral \[ I := \frac{1}{(2\pi i)^2} \int_{\Gamma_1}\int_{\Gamma_1} f(z,z') \frac{\zeta(1 + z + z')}{\zeta(1 + z)\zeta(1 + z')} \frac{R^{z + z'}}{z^2 z^{\prime 2}} dz dz'  \] obeys the estimate $$ I = f(0,0)\log R + \frac{\partial f}{\partial z'}(0,0) + \frac{1}{2\pi i} \int_{\Gamma_1} f(z,-z) \frac{dz}{\zeta(1 + z)\zeta(1 - z)z^4} + O_{m}(e^{-\delta \sqrt{\log R}})$$ for some $\delta = \delta(\sigma,\beta) > 0$ independent of $R$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP43.1
nodes.statement:
It is clear that $
u_{1/2}$ is non-negative and has expectation $1 + o(1)$.  To verify the linear forms condition \eqref{lfc}, we simply replace $
u$ by $(
u+1)/2$ in the definition and expand as a sum of $2^m$ terms, divided by $2^m$.  Since each term can be verified to be $1 + o(1)$ by the linear forms condition \eqref{lfc}, the claim follows.  The correlation condition is verified in a similar manner.  (A similar result holds for $(1-	heta) 
u + 	heta \vconst$ for any $0 \leq 	heta \leq 1$, but we will not need to use this generalization.)

nodes.name: Proof of LP43.2
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{ud-monotone} it suffices to prove the claim for $d=k-1$.  Raising to the power $2^{k-1}$, it suffices from \eqref{ud-def} to show that \[ \E igg( \prod_{\omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}} (
u(x + \omega \cdot h)-1) \;  igg| \; x \in \mathbb{Z}_N, h \in \mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1} igg) = o(1).\] The left-hand side can be expanded as  egin{equation} \sum_{A \subseteq \{0,1\}^{k-1}} (-1)^{|A|} \E igg( \prod_{\omega \in A} 
u(x + \omega \cdot h) \;  igg| \; x \in \mathbb{Z}_N, h \in \mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1}  igg).\end{equation} Let us look at the expression  egin{equation} \E igg( \prod_{\omega \in A} 
u(x + \omega \cdot h) \;  igg| \; x \in \mathbb{Z}_N, h \in \mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1}  igg) \end{equation} for some fixed $A \subseteq \{0,1\}^{k-1}$. This is of the form \[ \E\left(
u(\psi_1(\mathbf{x}))\dots 
u(\psi_{|A|}(\mathbf{x})) \; |\; \mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{Z}_N^kight),\] where $\mathbf{x} := (x,h_1,\dots,h_{k-1})$ and the $\psi_1, \ldots, \psi_{|A|}$ are some ordering of the $|A|$ linear forms $x + \omega \cdot h$, $\omega \in A$. It is clear that none of these forms is a rational multiple of any other. Thus we may invoke the $(2^{k-1},k,1)$-linear forms condition, which is a consequence of the fact that $
u$ is $k$-pseudorandom, to conclude that the expression \eqref{linear-forms-1} is $1 + o(1)$. Referring back to \eqref{eq5.1}, one sees that the claim now follows from the binomial theorem $\sum_{A \subseteq \{0,1\}^{k-1}} (-1)^{|A|} = (1-1)^{2^{k-1}} = 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of PrP43.3
nodes.statement:
By replacing $
u$ with $(
u+1)/2$ (and by dividing $f_j$ by 2), and using Lemma ef{halfway}, we see that we may in fact assume without loss of generality that we can improve \eqref{fj-bounds} to  egin{equation} |f_j(x)| \leq 
u(x) \hbox{ for all } x \in \mathbb{Z}_N, 0 \leq j \leq k-1. \end{equation} For similar reasons we may assume that $
u$ is strictly positive everywhere. By permuting the $f_j$ and $c_j$ if necessary, we may assume that the infimum \[ \inf_{0 \leq j \leq k-1} \| f_j \|_{U^{k-1}}\] is attained when $j=0$.  By shifting $x$ by $c_0 r$ if necessary we may assume that $c_0 = 0$. Our task is thus to show  egin{equation} \E igg( \prod_{j=0}^{k-1} f_j(x + c_j r) \;  igg| \; x,r \in \mathbb{Z}_N  igg) = O ig(\| f_0 \|_{U^{k-1}} ig) + o(1). \end{equation} The proof of this will fall into two parts. First of all we will use the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality $k - 1$ times (as is standard in the proof of theorems of this general type). In this way we will bound the left hand side of \eqref{gvn-task} by a 	extit{weighted} sum of $f_0$ over $(k-1)$-dimensional cubes. After that, we will show using the linear forms condition that these weights are roughly 1 on average, which will enable us to deduce \eqref{gvn-task}.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz $k-1$ times to weighted cube sum
nodes.statement: First of all we will use the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality $k - 1$ times (as is standard in the proof of theorems of this general type). In this way we will bound the left hand side of \eqref{gvn-task} by a \textit{weighted} sum of $f_0$ over $(k-1)$-dimensional cubes.

nodes.name: Weights are roughly 1 via linear forms condition
nodes.statement: After that, we will show using the linear forms condition that these weights are roughly 1 on average, which will enable us to deduce \eqref{gvn-task}.

nodes.name: Proof of LP43.3
nodes.statement:
Consider the quantity $J_d$. Since $\phi_{k-d-1}$ does not depend on $y_{k-d-1}$, we may take all quantities depending on $\phi_{k-d-1}$ outside of the $y_{k-d-1}$ average.  This allows us to write \[ J_d = \mathbb{E} ig( G(y,y')H(y,y')\;  ig|\; y_1,\dots,y_{k-d-2},y_{k-d},\dots,y_{k-1},y'_{k-d},\dots,y'_{k-1} \in \mathbb{Z}_N ig),\] where \[G(y,y') := \prod_{S \subseteq \{k-d,\dots,k-1\}}f_{k-d-1}(\phi_{k - d - 1}(y^{(S)})) 
u^{-1/2}(\phi_{k - d - 1}(y^{(S)})) \] and \[ H(y,y') := \mathbb{E} igg(\prod_{S \subseteq \{k-d,\dots,k-1\}} \prod_{i=0}^{k-d-2} f_i(\phi_i(y^{(S)})) \prod_{i=k - d - 1}^{k-1} 
u^{1/2}(\phi_i (y^{(S)})) \;  igg| \; y_{k - d - 1} \in \mathbb{Z}_N igg) \] (note we have multiplied and divided by several factors of the form $
u^{1/2}(\phi_{k-d-1}(y^{(S)})$).  Now apply Cauchy-Schwarz to give \[ |J_d|^2 \leq \mathbb{E}  ig(|G(y,y')|^2 \;  ig| \; y_1,\dots,y_{k-d-2},y_{k-d},\dots,y_{k-1},y'_{k-d},\dots,y'_{k-1} \in \mathbb{Z}_N ig) 	imes \] \[ \qquad \qquad	imes\mathbb{E}  ig(|H(y,y')|^2 \;  ig| \; y_1,\dots,y_{k-d-2},y_{k-d},\dots,y_{k-1},y'_{k-d},\dots,y'_{k-1} \in \mathbb{Z}_N ig).\] Since $|f_{k-d-1}(x)| \leq 
u(x)$ for all $x$, one sees from \eqref{alt-p-exp} that \[\mathbb{E}  ig(|G(y,y')|^2 \;  ig| \; y_1,\dots,y_{k-d-2},y_{k-d},\dots,y_{k-1},y'_{k-d},\dots,y'_{k-1} \in \mathbb{Z}_N ig) \leq P_{d}\] (note that the $y_{k-d-1}$ averaging in \eqref{alt-p-exp} is redundant since $\phi_{k-d-1}$ does not depend on this variable). Moreover, by writing in the definition of $H(y,y')$ and expanding out the square, replacing the averaging variable $y_{k - d - 1}$ with the new variables $y_{k - d - 1}, y'_{k - d - 1}$, one sees from \eqref{j-def} that \[  \mathbb{E}  ig(|H(y,y')|^2 \;  ig| \; y_1,\dots,y_{k-d-2},y_{k-d},\dots,y_{k-1},y'_{k-d},\dots,y'_{k-1} \in \mathbb{Z}_N ig) = J_{d+1}.\] The claim follows.

nodes.name: Proof of LP43.4
nodes.statement: Expanding out the square, it then suffices to show that \[  \E\bigg( W(x,h)^q \prod_{\omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}} \nu(x + \omega \cdot h) \; \bigg| \; x \in \mathbb{Z}_N, h \in \mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1} \bigg) = 1 + o(1)\] for $q=0,1,2$. This can be achieved by three applications of the linear forms condition, as follows:\\[11pt] $q = 0$. Use the $(2^{k-1},k,1)$-linear forms property with variables $x,h_1,\dots,h_{k-1}$ and forms \[ x + \omega \cdot h \qquad \omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}.\] $q = 1$. Use the $(2^{k-2}(k+1), 2k - 2, k)$-linear forms property with variables $x$, $h_1,\dots,h_{k-1}$, $y_1,\dots,y_{k-2}$ and forms \begin{eqnarray*} \phi_i(y + \omega h) & & \omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}, \;\; \omega_i = 0, 1 \leq i \leq k - 1;\\ x + \omega \cdot h, && \omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}.\end{eqnarray*} $q = 2$. Use the $(k\cdot 2^{k-1}, 3k - 4, k)$-linear forms property with variables $x$, $h_1,\dots,h_{k-1}$, $y_1,\dots,y_{k-2}$, $y'_1,\dots,y'_{k-2}$ and forms \begin{eqnarray*} \phi_i(y + \omega h) && \omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1},\;\; \omega_i = 0, 1 \leq i \leq k - 1;\\ \phi_i(y' + \omega h) && \omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1},\;\; \omega_i = 0, 1 \leq i \leq k - 1;\\ x + \omega \cdot h, && \omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}.\end{eqnarray*} Here of course we adopt the convention that $y_{k-1} = x - y_1 - \ldots - y_{k-2}$ and $y'_{k-1} = x - y'_1 - \ldots - y'_{k-2}$. This completes the proof of the lemma, and hence of Proposition \ref{vn}.

nodes.name: Case $q=0$
nodes.statement: $q = 0$. Use the $(2^{k-1},k,1)$-linear forms property with variables $x,h_1,\dots,h_{k-1}$ and forms \[ x + \omega \cdot h \qquad \omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}.\]

nodes.name: Case $q=1$
nodes.statement: $q = 1$. Use the $(2^{k-2}(k+1), 2k - 2, k)$-linear forms property with variables $x$, $h_1,\dots,h_{k-1}$, $y_1,\dots,y_{k-2}$ and forms \begin{eqnarray*} \phi_i(y + \omega h) & & \omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}, \;\; \omega_i = 0, 1 \leq i \leq k - 1;\\ x + \omega \cdot h, && \omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}.\end{eqnarray*}

nodes.name: Case $q=2$
nodes.statement: $q = 2$. Use the $(k\cdot 2^{k-1}, 3k - 4, k)$-linear forms property with variables $x$, $h_1,\dots,h_{k-1}$, $y_1,\dots,y_{k-2}$, $y'_1,\dots,y'_{k-2}$ and forms \begin{eqnarray*} \phi_i(y + \omega h) && \omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1},\;\; \omega_i = 0, 1 \leq i \leq k - 1;\\ \phi_i(y' + \omega h) && \omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1},\;\; \omega_i = 0, 1 \leq i \leq k - 1;\\ x + \omega \cdot h, && \omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}.\end{eqnarray*}

nodes.name: Proof of LP43.5
nodes.statement:
The identity \eqref{dual-first} is clear just by expanding out both sides using \eqref{cald}, \eqref{ud-def}.  To prove \eqref{dual} we may of course assume $F$ is not identically zero.  By \eqref{dual-def} and \eqref{dual-first} it suffices to show that $$ |\langle f, {\mathcal D} F angle| \leq \|f\|_{U^{k-1}} \| F \|_{U^{k-1}}^{2^{k-1}-1}$$ for arbitrary functions $f$.  But by \eqref{cald} the left-hand side is simply the Gowers inner product $\langle (f_\omega)_{\omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}} angle_{U^{k-1}}$, where $f_\omega := f$ when $\omega = 0$ and $f_\omega := F$ otherwise.  The claim then follows from the Gowers Cauchy-Schwarz inequality \eqref{gcz}. Finally, we observe that \eqref{dual-bounded} is a consequence of the linear forms condition.  Bounding $F$ by $2 (
u+1)/2 = 2 
u_{1/2}$, it suffices to show that $$ {\mathcal D} 
u_{1/2}(x) \leq 1 + o(1) $$ uniformly in the choice of $x \in \mathbb{Z}_N$.  The left-hand side can be expanded using \eqref{cald} as $$ \E igg( \prod_{\omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}: \omega 
eq 0^{k-1}} 
u_{1/2}(x + \omega \cdot h) \;  igg| \;  h \in \mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1}  igg).$$ By the linear forms condition \eqref{lfc} (and Lemma ef{halfway}) this expression is $1 + o(1)$ (this is the only place in the paper that we appeal to the linear forms condition in the non-homogeneous case where some $b_i 
eq 0$; here, all the $b_i$ are equal to $x$).  Note that \eqref{example-2} corresponds to the $k=3$ case of this application of the linear forms condition.

nodes.name: Identity for $\langle F,\mathcal{D}F\rangle$
nodes.statement: The identity \eqref{dual-first} is clear just by expanding out both sides using \eqref{cald}, \eqref{ud-def}.

nodes.name: Dual norm identity via Gowers Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: To prove \eqref{dual} we may of course assume $F$ is not identically zero.  By \eqref{dual-def} and \eqref{dual-first} it suffices to show that $$ |\langle f, {\mathcal D} F \rangle| \leq \|f\|_{U^{k-1}} \| F \|_{U^{k-1}}^{2^{k-1}-1}$$ for arbitrary functions $f$.  But by \eqref{cald} the left-hand side is simply the Gowers inner product $\langle (f_\omega)_{\omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}} \rangle_{U^{k-1}}$, where $f_\omega := f$ when $\omega = 0$ and $f_\omega := F$ otherwise.  The claim then follows from the Gowers Cauchy-Schwarz inequality \eqref{gcz}.

nodes.name: $L^\infty$ bound via linear forms condition
Proof of LP43.6
nodes.statement:
By linearity it suffices to prove this when $P$ is a monomial. By enlarging $K$ to at most $dK$ and repeating the functions $F_j$ as necessary, it in fact suffices to prove this for the monomial $P(x_1,\ldots,x_K) = x_1 \ldots x_K$. Recalling the definition of $(U^{k-1})^*$, we are thus required to show that \[  ig\langle f, \prod_{j=1}^K {\mathcal D} F_j  igangle = O_K(1) \] for all $f: \mathbb{Z}_N 	o \R$ satisfying $\| f \|_{U^{k-1}} \leq 1$.  By \eqref{cald} the left-hand side can be expanded as \[ \E igg( f(x) \prod_{j=1}^K \E ig( \prod_{\omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}: \omega 
eq 0^{k-1}} F_j(x + \omega \cdot h^{(j)}) \;   ig| \;  h^{(j)} \in \mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1}  ig) \;  igg|\; x \in \mathbb{Z}_N igg).\] We can make the change of variables $h^{(j)} = h + H^{(j)}$ for any $h \in \mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1}$, and then average over $h$, to rewrite this as \[ \E igg( f(x) \prod_{j=1}^K \E ig( \prod_{\omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}: \omega 
eq 0^{k-1}} F_j(x + \omega \cdot H^{(j)} + \omega \cdot h) \;  ig| \; H^{(j)} \in \mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1}  ig) \;  igg| \; x \in \mathbb{Z}_N; h \in \mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1} igg).\] Expanding the $j$ product and interchanging the expectations, we can rewrite this in terms of the Gowers inner product as \[ \E ig( \langle (f_{\omega, H})_{\omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}} angle_{U^{k-1}} \;  ig| \; H \in (\mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1})^K  ig)\] where $H := (H^{(1)}, \ldots, H^{(K)})$, $f_{0,H} := f$, and $f_{\omega,H} := g_{\omega \cdot H}$ for $\omega 
eq 0^{k-1}$, where $\omega \cdot H := (\omega \cdot H^{(1)}, \ldots, \omega \cdot H^{(K)})$ and  egin{equation} g_{u^{(1)}, \ldots, u^{(K)}}(x) := \prod_{j=1}^K F_j(x + u^{(j)}) \hbox{ for all } u^{(1)}, \ldots, u^{(K)} \in \mathbb{Z}_N. \end{equation} By the Gowers-Cauchy-Schwarz inequality \eqref{gcz} we can bound this as \[ \E igg( \| f\|_{U^{k-1}} \prod_{\omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}: \omega 
eq 0^{k-1}} \| g_{\omega \cdot H} \|_{U^{k-1}} \;  igg| \; H \in (\mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1})^K  igg)\] so to prove the claim it will suffice to show that \[ \E igg( \prod_{\omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}: \omega 
eq 0^{k-1}} \| g_{\omega \cdot H} \|_{U^{k-1}} \;  igg| \; H \in (\mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1})^K  igg) = O_K(1).\] By H"older's inequality it will suffice to show that $$\E ig( \| g_{\omega \cdot H} \|_{U^{k-1}}^{2^{k-1}-1} \;  ig| \; H \in (\mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1})^K  ig) = O_K(1)$$ for each $\omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}  ackslash 0^{k-1}$. Fix $\omega$.  Since $2^{k-1}-1 \leq 2^{k-1}$, another application of H"older's inequality shows that it in fact suffices to show that $$\E ig( \| g_{\omega \cdot H} \|_{U^{k-1}}^{2^{k-1}} \;  ig| \; H \in (\mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1})^K  ig) = O_K(1).$$ Since $\omega 
eq 0^{k-1}$, the map $H \mapsto \omega \cdot H$ is a uniform covering of $\mathbb{Z}_N^K$ by $(\mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1})^K$.  Thus by \eqref{uniform-cover} we can rewrite the left-hand side as $$\E ig( \| g_{u^{(1)}, \ldots, u^{(K)}} \|_{U^{k-1}}^{2^{k-1}} \;  ig| \; u^{(1)}, \ldots, u^{(K)} \in \mathbb{Z}_N  ig).$$ Expanding this out using \eqref{ud-def} and \eqref{foh-def}, we can rewrite the left-hand side as $$\E igg( \prod_{	ilde \omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}} \prod_{j=1}^K F_j(x + u^{(j)} + h \cdot 	ilde \omega) \;  igg| \; x \in \mathbb{Z}_N, h \in \mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1}, u^{(1)}, \ldots, u^{(K)} \in \mathbb{Z}_N  igg).$$ This factorises as $$ \E igg( \prod_{j=1}^K \E ig( \prod_{	ilde \omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}} F_j(x + u^{(j)} + h \cdot 	ilde \omega) \;  ig| \; u^{(j)} \in \mathbb{Z}_N  ig) \;  igg| \; x \in \mathbb{Z}_N, h \in \mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1}  igg).$$ Applying \eqref{fjb-better}, we reduce to showing that $$ \E igg( \E ig( \prod_{	ilde \omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}} 
u(x + u + h \cdot 	ilde \omega)\;  ig| \; u \in \mathbb{Z}_N  ig)^K \;  igg| \; x \in \mathbb{Z}_N, h \in \mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1}  igg) = O_K(1).$$ We can make the change of variables $y := x+u$, and then discard the redundant $x$ averaging, to reduce to showing that $$ \E igg( \E ig( \prod_{	ilde \omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}} 
u(y + h \cdot 	ilde \omega) \;  ig| \; y \in \mathbb{Z}_N  ig)^K \;  igg| \; h \in \mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1}  igg) = O_K(1).$$ Now we are ready to apply the correlation condition (Definition ef{correlation-condition}). This is, in fact, the only time we will use that condition. It gives \[ \E igg( \prod_{	ilde \omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}} 
u(y + h \cdot 	ilde \omega) \;  igg| \; y \in \mathbb{Z}_N igg) \leq \sum_{	ilde \omega, 	ilde \omega' \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}: 	ilde \omega 
eq 	ilde \omega'} 	au(h \cdot (	ilde \omega - 	ilde \omega'))\] where, recall, $	au$ is a weight function satisfying $\mathbb{E}(	au^q) = O_q(1)$ for all $q$. Applying the triangle inequality in $L^K(\Z_N^{k-1})$, it thus suffices to show that \[ \E ig( 	au(h \cdot (	ilde \omega - 	ilde \omega'))^K \;  ig| \; h \in \mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1}  ig) = O_K(1)\] for all distinct $	ilde \omega, 	ilde \omega' \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}$.  But the map $h \mapsto h \cdot (	ilde \omega - 	ilde \omega')$ is a uniform covering of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ by $(\mathbb{Z}_N)^{k-1}$, so by \eqref{uniform-cover} the left-hand side is just $\E(	au^K) $, which is $O_K(1)$.

nodes.name: Reduce to the monomial $x_1\ldots x_K$
nodes.statement: By linearity it suffices to prove this when $P$ is a monomial. By enlarging $K$ to at most $dK$ and repeating the functions $F_j$ as necessary, it in fact suffices to prove this for the monomial $P(x_1,\ldots,x_K) = x_1 \ldots x_K$. Recalling the definition of $(U^{k-1})^*$, we are thus required to show that \[ \big\langle f, \prod_{j=1}^K {\mathcal D} F_j \big\rangle = O_K(1) \] for all $f: \mathbb{Z}_N \to \R$ satisfying $\| f \|_{U^{k-1}} \leq 1$.

nodes.name: Gowers-Cauchy-Schwarz and H\"older reductions
nodes.statement: By the Gowers-Cauchy-Schwarz inequality \eqref{gcz} we can bound this as \[ \E\bigg( \| f\|_{U^{k-1}} \prod_{\omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}: \omega \neq 0^{k-1}} \| g_{\omega \cdot H} \|_{U^{k-1}} \; \bigg| \; H \in (\mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1})^K \bigg)\] so to prove the claim it will suffice to show that \[ \E\bigg( \prod_{\omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}: \omega \neq 0^{k-1}} \| g_{\omega \cdot H} \|_{U^{k-1}} \; \bigg| \; H \in (\mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1})^K \bigg) = O_K(1).\] By H\"older's inequality it will suffice to show that $$\E\big( \| g_{\omega \cdot H} \|_{U^{k-1}}^{2^{k-1}-1} \; \big| \; H \in (\mathbb{Z}_N^{k-1})^K \big) = O_K(1)$$ for each $\omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1} \backslash 0^{k-1}$.

nodes.name: Apply the correlation condition
nodes.statement: Now we are ready to apply the correlation condition (Definition \ref{correlation-condition}). This is, in fact, the only time we will use that condition. It gives \[ \E\bigg( \prod_{\tilde \omega \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}} \nu(y + h \cdot \tilde \omega) \; \bigg| \; y \in \mathbb{Z}_N\bigg) \leq \sum_{\tilde \omega, \tilde \omega' \in \{0,1\}^{k-1}: \tilde \omega \neq \tilde \omega'} \tau(h \cdot (\tilde \omega - \tilde \omega'))\] where, recall, $\tau$ is a weight function satisfying $\mathbb{E}(\tau^q) = O_q(1)$ for all $q$.

nodes.name: Proof of PrP43.4
nodes.statement:
Let $\Phi$, $\psi$ be as in the Proposition, and let $\eps > 0$ be arbitrary.  From \eqref{dual-bounded} we know that the basic Gowers anti-uniform functions ${\mathcal D} F_1, \ldots, {\mathcal D} F_K$ take values in the compact interval $I := [-2^{2^{k-1}}, 2^{2^{k-1}}]$ introduced earlier.  By the Weierstrass approximation theorem, we can thus find a polynomial $P$ (depending only on $K$ and $\eps$) such that $$ \| \Phi({\mathcal D} F_1, \ldots, {\mathcal D} F_K) - P({\mathcal D} F_1, \ldots, {\mathcal D} F_K) \|_{L^\infty} \leq \eps$$ and thus by \eqref{numean} and taking absolute values inside the inner product, we have $$ |\langle 
u - 1, \Phi({\mathcal D} F_1, \ldots, {\mathcal D} F_K) - P({\mathcal D} F_1, \ldots, {\mathcal D} F_K) angle| \leq (2 + o(1)) \eps.$$ On the other hand, from Lemma ef{poly-lemma}, Lemma ef{mua} and \eqref{dual-def} we have $$ \langle 
u - 1, P({\mathcal D} F_1, \ldots, {\mathcal D} F_K) angle = o_{K,\eps}(1)$$ since $P$ depends on $K$ and $\eps$. Combining the two estimates we thus see that for $N$ sufficiently large (depending on $K$ and $\eps$) we have $$ |\langle 
u - 1, \Phi({\mathcal D} F_1, \ldots, {\mathcal D} F_K) angle| \leq 4\eps$$ (for instance). Since $\eps > 0$ was arbitrary, the claim follows.  It is clear that this argument also gives the uniform bounds when $\Phi$ ranges over a compact set (by covering this compact set by finitely many balls of radius $\eps$ in the uniform topology).

nodes.name: Polynomial approximation via Weierstrass
nodes.statement: By the Weierstrass approximation theorem, we can thus find a polynomial $P$ (depending only on $K$ and $\eps$) such that $$ \| \Phi({\mathcal D} F_1, \ldots, {\mathcal D} F_K) - P({\mathcal D} F_1, \ldots, {\mathcal D} F_K) \|_{L^\infty} \leq \eps$$ and thus by \eqref{numean} and taking absolute values inside the inner product, we have $$ |\langle \nu - 1, \Phi({\mathcal D} F_1, \ldots, {\mathcal D} F_K) - P({\mathcal D} F_1, \ldots, {\mathcal D} F_K) \rangle| \leq (2 + o(1)) \eps.$$

nodes.name: Combine with polynomial estimate
nodes.statement: On the other hand, from Lemma \ref{poly-lemma}, Lemma \ref{mua} and \eqref{dual-def} we have $$ \langle \nu - 1, P({\mathcal D} F_1, \ldots, {\mathcal D} F_K) \rangle = o_{K,\eps}(1)$$ since $P$ depends on $K$ and $\eps$. Combining the two estimates we thus see that for $N$ sufficiently large (depending on $K$ and $\eps$) we have $$ |\langle \nu - 1, \Phi({\mathcal D} F_1, \ldots, {\mathcal D} F_K) \rangle| \leq 4\eps$$ (for instance).

nodes.name: Proof of PrP43.5
nodes.statement:
Observe from Fubini's theorem and \eqref{numean} that $$ \int_0^1 \sum_{n \in \Z} \E ig( { f 1}_{G(x) \in [\eps(n-\eta+\alpha), \eps(n+\eta+\alpha)]} (
u(x)+1) \;  ig| \; x \in \Z_N  ig)\ d\alpha = 2\eta \E( 
u(x)+1 | x \in \Z_N ) = O(\eta) $$ and hence by the pigeonhole principle there exists $0 \leq \alpha \leq 1$ such that  egin{equation} \sum_{n \in \Z} \E ig( { f 1}_{G(x) \in [\eps(n-\eta+\alpha), \eps(n+\eta+\alpha)]} (
u(x)+1) \;  ig| \; x \in \Z_N  ig) = O( \eta ). \end{equation} We now set $\B_{\eps,\eta}(G)$ to be the $\sigma$-algebra whose atoms are the sets $G^{-1}([\eps (n+\alpha), \eps(n+1+\alpha)))$ for $n \in \Z$.  This is well-defined since the intervals $[\eps (n+\alpha), \eps(n+1+\alpha))$ tile the real line. It is clear that if $\B$ is an arbitrary $\sigma$-algebra, then on any atom of $\B \vee \B_{\eps,\eta}(G)$, the function $G$ takes values in an interval of diameter $\eps$, which yields \eqref{trivial}.  Now we verify the approximation by continuous functions property.  Let $A := G^{-1}([\eps (n+\alpha), \eps(n+1+\alpha)))$ be an atom. Since $G$ takes values in $I$, we may assume that $n = O(1/\eps)$, since $A$ is empty otherwise; note that this already establishes the bounded complexity property.  Let $\psi_\eta: \R 	o [0,1]$ be a fixed continuous cutoff function which equals 1 on $[\eta, 1-\eta]$ and vanishes outside of $[-\eta,1+\eta]$, and define $\Psi_A(x) := \psi_\eta(  rac{x}{\eps} - n - \alpha )$.  Then it is clear that $\Psi_A$ ranges over a compact subset $E_{\eps,\eta}$ of $C^0(I)$ (because $n$ and $\alpha$ are bounded).  Furthermore from \eqref{dual-shift} it is clear that we have \eqref{nup-bound}.  The claim follows.

nodes.name: Construct the $\sigma$-algebra via pigeonhole
nodes.statement:
Observe from Fubini's theorem and \eqref{numean} that $$ \int_0^1 \sum_{n \in \Z} \E ig( { f 1}_{G(x) \in [\eps(n-\eta+\alpha), \eps(n+\eta+\alpha)]} (
u(x)+1) \;  ig| \; x \in \Z_N  ig)\ d\alpha = 2\eta \E( 
u(x)+1 | x \in \Z_N ) = O(\eta) $$ and hence by the pigeonhole principle there exists $0 \leq \alpha \leq 1$ such that  egin{equation} \sum_{n \in \Z} \E ig( { f 1}_{G(x) \in [\eps(n-\eta+\alpha), \eps(n+\eta+\alpha)]} (
u(x)+1) \;  ig| \; x \in \Z_N  ig) = O( \eta ). \end{equation} We now set $\B_{\eps,\eta}(G)$ to be the $\sigma$-algebra whose atoms are the sets $G^{-1}([\eps (n+\alpha), \eps(n+1+\alpha)))$ for $n \in \Z$.

nodes.name: Verify approximation by continuous functions
nodes.statement: Now we verify the approximation by continuous functions property.  Let $A := G^{-1}([\eps (n+\alpha), \eps(n+1+\alpha)))$ be an atom. Since $G$ takes values in $I$, we may assume that $n = O(1/\eps)$, since $A$ is empty otherwise; note that this already establishes the bounded complexity property.  Let $\psi_\eta: \R \to [0,1]$ be a fixed continuous cutoff function which equals 1 on $[\eta, 1-\eta]$ and vanishes outside of $[-\eta,1+\eta]$, and define $\Psi_A(x) := \psi_\eta( \frac{x}{\eps} - n - \alpha )$.  Then it is clear that $\Psi_A$ ranges over a compact subset $E_{\eps,\eta}$ of $C^0(I)$ (because $n$ and $\alpha$ are bounded).  Furthermore from \eqref{dual-shift} it is clear that we have \eqref{nup-bound}.  The claim follows.

nodes.name: Proof of PrP43.6
nodes.statement:
The claim \eqref{trivial-specific} follows immediately from \eqref{trivial}.  Now we prove \eqref{mok-small} and \eqref{unif-mu}. Since each of the $\B_{\eps,\eta}(\D F_j)$ are generated by $O(1/\eps)$ atoms, we see that $\B$ is generated by $O_{K,\eps}(1)$ atoms. Call an atom $A$ of $\B$ \emph{small} if $\E( (
u + 1) { f 1}_A) \leq \eta^{1/2}$, and let $\Omega$ be the union of all the small atoms.  Then clearly $\Omega$ lies in $\B$ and obeys \eqref{mok-small}.  To prove the remaining claim \eqref{unif-mu}, it suffices to show that  egin{equation}  rac{ \E( (
u - 1) { f 1}_A ) }{ \E( { f 1}_A ) } = \E( 
u - 1 | A ) = o_{K,\eps,\eta}(1) + O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}) \end{equation} for all atoms $A$ in $\B$ which are not small.  However, by definition of ``small'' we have $$ \E( (
u - 1) { f 1}_A ) + 2 \E( { f 1}_A ) = \E( (
u+1) { f 1}_A ) \geq \eta^{1/2}.$$ Thus to complete the proof of \eqref{sigma-smooth} it will suffice (since $\eta$ is small and $N$ is large) to show that  egin{equation} \E( (
u - 1) { f 1}_A ) = o_{K,\eps,\eta}(1) + O_{K,\eps}(\eta). \end{equation} On the other hand, since $A$ is the intersection of $K$ atoms $A_1, \ldots, A_K$ from $\B_{\eps,\eta}(\D F_1), \ldots$, $\B_{\eps,\eta}(\D F_K)$ respectively, we see from Proposition ef{sigma-gen} and an easy induction argument (involving H"older's inequality and the triangle inequality) that we can find a continuous function $\Psi_A: I^K 	o [0,1]$ such that $$\| (
u + 1) ({ f 1}_A - \Psi_A(\D F_1, \ldots, \D F_K)) \|_{L^1(\Z_N)} = O_K(\eta),$$ so in particular $$ \| (
u - 1) ({ f 1}_A - \Psi_A(\D F_1, \ldots, \D F_K)) \|_{L^1(\Z_N)} = O_K(\eta).$$ Furthermore one can easily ensure that $\Psi_A$ lives in a compact set $E_{\eps,\eta,K}$ of $C^0(I^K)$.  From this and Proposition ef{weier} we have $$ \E( (
u - 1) \Psi_A(\D F_1, \ldots, \D F_K)) ) = o_{K,\eps,\eta}(1)$$ since $N$ is assumed large depending in $K,\eps,\eta$, and the claim \eqref{nubf} now follows from the triangle inequality.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{main} assuming Proposition \ref{kvn-decomp}
nodes.statement:
Let $f$, $\delta$ be as in Theorem ef{main}, and let $0 < \eps \ll \delta$ be a parameter to be chosen later.  Let $\B$ be as in the above decomposition, and write $ unif := (1-{ f 1}_\Omega)(f-\E(f|\B))$ and $ anti := (1-{ f 1}_\Omega)\E(f|\B)$ (the subscript $U$ stands for Gowers uniform, and $U^\perp$ for Gowers anti-uniform).  Observe from \eqref{small-exceptions-final}, \eqref{f-bound-2}, \eqref{f-density} and the measurability of $\Omega$ that $$ \E(  anti ) = \E( (1-{ f 1}_\Omega) f) \geq \E(f) - \E( 
u { f 1}_\Omega ) \geq \delta - o_\eps(1).$$ Also, by \eqref{mu-regular-final} we see that $ anti$ is bounded above by $1+o_{\eps}(1)$.  Since $f$ is non-negative, $ anti$ is also. We may thus apply Proposition ef{sz}  to obtain \[ \E ig(  anti(x)  anti(x+r) \ldots  anti(x+(k-1)r) \;  ig| \; x,r \in \mathbb{Z}_N  ig) \geq c(k,\delta) -  o_{\eps}(1) - o_{k,\delta}(1).\] On the other hand, from \eqref{unif-ok} we have $\| unif \|_{U^{k-1}} \leq \eps^{1/2^k}$; since $(1-{ f 1}_\Omega)f$ is bounded by $
u$ and $ anti$ is bounded by $1+o_{\eps}(1)$, we thus see that $ unif$ is pointwise bounded by $
u+1+o_{\eps}(1)$. Applying the generalised von Neumann theorem (Proposition ef{vn}) we thus see that \[ \E ig( f_0(x) f_1(x+r) \ldots f_{k-1}(x+(k-1)r) \;  ig| \; x,r \in \mathbb{Z}_N  ig) = O(\eps^{1/2^k}) + o_{\eps}(1)\] whenever each $f_j$ is equal to $ unif$ or $ anti$, with at least one $f_j$ equal to $ unif$.  Adding these two estimates together we obtain \[ \E( 	ilde f(x) 	ilde f(x+r) \ldots 	ilde f(x+(k-1)r) | x,r \in \mathbb{Z}_N ) \geq c(k,\delta) - O(\eps^{1/2^k}) - o_{\eps}(1) - o_{k,\delta}(1),\] where $	ilde f :=  unif +  anti = (1-{ f 1}_\Omega) f$.  But since $0 \leq (1-{ f 1}_\Omega) f \leq f$ we obtain $$ \E( f(x) f(x+r) \ldots f(x+(k-1)r) | x,r \in \mathbb{Z}_N ) \geq c(k,\delta) - O(\eps^{1/2^k}) - o_{\eps}(1)- o_{k,\delta}(1).$$ Since $\eps$ can be made arbitrarily small (as long as $N$ is taken sufficiently large), the error terms on the right-hand side can be taken to be arbitrarily small by choosing $N$ sufficiently large depending on $k$ and $\delta$.  The claim follows.
nodes.section: A Furstenberg tower, and the proof of Theorem \ref{main}

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition \ref{kvn-decomp} assuming Proposition \ref{relative}
nodes.statement: Fix $\eps$, and let $K_0$ be the smallest integer greater than $2^{2^k}/\eps+1$; this quantity will be the upper bound for the number of iterations of an algorithm which we shall give shortly.  We shall need a parameter $0 < \eta \ll \eps$ which we shall choose later (we assume $\eta < \eta_0(\eps, K_0)$, and then we shall assume $N > N_0(\eta,\eps)$ is sufficiently large. To construct $\B$ and $\Omega$ we shall, for some $K \in [0,K_0]$, iteratively construct a sequence of basic Gowers anti-uniform functions $\D F_1, \ldots, \D F_K$ on $\mathbb{Z}_N$ together with exceptional sets $\Omega_0 \subseteq\Omega_1 \subseteq\ldots \subseteq\Omega_K \subseteq\mathbb{Z}_N$ in the following manner. \begin{itemize} \item Step 0.  Initialise $K = 0$ and $\Omega_0 := \emptyset$.  (We will later increment the value of $K$). \item Step 1.  Let $\B_K$ and $F_{K+1}$ be defined by \eqref{BK-def} and \eqref{FK1-def} respectively.  Thus for instance when $K=0$ we will have $\B_0 = \{\emptyset,\Z_N\}$ and $F_1 = f - \E(f)$.  Observe that in the $K=0$ case, the estimates \eqref{f-disc-ok}, \eqref{om-small}, \eqref{uniform-dist} are trivial (the latter bound following from \eqref{numean}).  As we shall see, these three estimates will be preserved throughout the algorithm. \item Step 2.  If the estimate \eqref{non-terminate} \emph{fails}, or in other words that $$ \| F_{K+1} \|_{U^{k-1}} \leq \eps^{1/2^k},$$ then we set $\Omega := \Omega_K$ and $\B := \B_K$, and successfully terminate the algorithm. \item Step 3.  If instead \eqref{non-terminate} holds, then we define $\B_{K+1}$ by \eqref{BK1-def}.  (Here we of course need $K \leq K_0$, but this will be guaranteed by Step 4 below).  We then invoke Proposition \ref{relative} to locate an exceptional set $\Omega_{K+1} \supset \Omega_K$ in $\B_{K+1}$ obeying the conditions \eqref{om-small-2}, \eqref{uniform-dist-2}, and for which we have the energy increment property \eqref{fj-increment}.  Also, we have \eqref{f-disc-ok-2}. \item Step 4.  Increment $K$ to $K+1$; observe from construction that the estimates \eqref{f-disc-ok}, \eqref{om-small}, \eqref{uniform-dist} will be preserved when doing so.  If we now have $K > K_0$, then we terminate the algorithm with an error; otherwise, return to Step 1. \end{itemize} Assuming Proposition \ref{relative}, we see that this algorithm will terminate after finitely many steps with one of two outcomes: either it will terminate successfully in Step 2 for some $K \leq K_0$, or else it will terminate with an error in Step 4 when $K$ exceeds $K_0$.  Assume for the moment that the former case occurs.  Then it is clear that at the successful conclusion of this algorithm, we will have generated a $\sigma$-algebra $\B$ and an exceptional set $\Omega$ with the properties required for Proposition \ref{kvn-decomp}, with error terms of $O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2})$ instead of $o_\eps(1)$, if $N > N_0(\eta, K, \eps)$. But by making $\eta$ decay sufficiently slowly to zero, we can replace the $O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2})$ bounds by $o_\eps(1)$; note that the dependence of the error terms on $K$ will not be relevant since $K$ is bounded by $K_0$, which depends only on $\eps$. To conclude the proof of Proposition \ref{kvn-decomp} it will thus suffice to show that the above algorithm does not terminate with an error.  Suppose for a contradiction that the algorithm ran until the $K_0^{\mbox{\scriptsize th}}$ iteration before terminating with an error in Step 4. Then if we define the energies $E_K$ for $0 \leq K \leq K_0+1$ by the formula $$ E_K := \| (1 - {\bf 1}_{\Omega_K}) \E(f|\B_K) \|_{L^2(\Z_N)}^2$$ then we see from \eqref{fj-increment} that \begin{equation} E_{K+1} \geq E_K + 2^{-2^k + 1} \eps \hbox{ for all } 0 \leq K \leq K_0 \end{equation} (for instance).  Also, by \eqref{fbk-bound} we have $$ 0 \leq E_K \leq 1 + O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}) \hbox{ for all } 0 \leq K \leq K_0.$$ If $\eta < \eta_0(K,\eps)$ is sufficiently small, these last two statements contradict one another for $K = K_0$. Thus the above algorithm cannot reach the $K_0^{\mbox{\scriptsize th}}$ iteration, and instead terminates successfully at Step 2.  This completes the proof of Proposition \ref{kvn-decomp}.

nodes.name: Step 0: initialise
nodes.statement: Step 0.  Initialise $K = 0$ and $\Omega_0 := \emptyset$.  (We will later increment the value of $K$).

nodes.name: Step 1: define $\B_K$ and $F_{K+1}$

Thus for instance when $K=0$ we will have $\B_0 = \{\emptyset,\Z_N\}$ and $F_1 = f - \E(f)$. As we shall see, these three estimates will be preserved throughout the algorithm.

nodes.name: Step 2: termination test
nodes.statement: Step 2.  If the estimate \eqref{non-terminate} \emph{fails}, or in other words that $$ \| F_{K+1} \|_{U^{k-1}} \leq \eps^{1/2^k},$$ then we set $\Omega := \Omega_K$ and $\B := \B_K$, and successfully terminate the algorithm.

nodes.name: Step 3: refine $\sigma$-algebra via Proposition relative
nodes.statement: Step 3.  If instead \eqref{non-terminate} holds, then we define $\B_{K+1}$ by \eqref{BK1-def}.  (Here we of course need $K \leq K_0$, but this will be guaranteed by Step 4 below).  We then invoke Proposition \ref{relative} to locate an exceptional set $\Omega_{K+1} \supset \Omega_K$ in $\B_{K+1}$ obeying the conditions \eqref{om-small-2}, \eqref{uniform-dist-2}, and for which we have the energy increment property \eqref{fj-increment}.  Also, we have \eqref{f-disc-ok-2}.

nodes.name: Step 4: increment and loop
nodes.statement: Step 4.  Increment $K$ to $K+1$; observe from construction that the estimates \eqref{f-disc-ok}, \eqref{om-small}, \eqref{uniform-dist} will be preserved when doing so.  If we now have $K > K_0$, then we terminate the algorithm with an error; otherwise, return to Step 1.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition \ref{relative}
nodes.statement:
Let $
u$, $f$, $K$, $\eps$, $\eta$, $F_1,\ldots,F_K, F_{K+1}$, $\B_K$, $\Omega_K$, $\B_{K+1}$ be as in the proposition.  We begin by proving the bounds \eqref{fbk-bound}, \eqref{f-disc-ok-2}.  From \eqref{uniform-dist} we have $$ \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K}}) \E( 
u | \B_{K} )\|_{L^\infty} \leq 1 + O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2});$$ since $f$ is non-negative and bounded pointwise by $
u$, we obtain \eqref{fbk-bound}.  The bound \eqref{f-disc-ok-2} then follows from \eqref{fbk-bound} and \eqref{FK1-def}, where we again use that $f$ is non-negative and bounded pointwise by $
u$. This shows in particular that $\D F_1, \ldots$, $\D F_{K_1+1}$ are basic Gowers anti-uniform functions (up to multiplicative errors of $1 + O_{K_1,\eps}(\eta^{1/2})$, which are negligible). Applying Lemma ef{antiuniform} (scaling out the multiplicative error of $1 + O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2})$) and using \eqref{f-disc-ok} and \eqref{f-disc-ok-2} we conclude that  egin{equation} \| \D F_j \|_{L^\infty(\Z_N)} \leq 2^{2^{k-1}-1} + O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}) \hbox{ for all } 0 \leq j \leq K+1, \end{equation} since we are assuming $N$ to be large depending on $K$, $\eps$, $\eta$. We now apply Proposition ef{bohr-sigma} (absorbing the multiplicative errors of $1+O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2})$) to conclude that we may find a set $\Omega$ in $\B_{K+1}$ such that $$ \E( (
u + 1) { f 1}_{\Omega} ) = O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2})$$ and $$ \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega}) \E(
u - 1 | \B_{K+1}) \|_{L^\infty} = O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}).$$ If we then set $\Omega_{K+1} := \Omega_K \cup \Omega$, then we can verify \eqref{om-small-2} and \eqref{uniform-dist-2} from \eqref{om-small} and \eqref{uniform-dist}. It remains to verify \eqref{fj-increment}, the energy increment property, that is to say the statement  egin{equation} \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) \E(f|\B_{K+1}) \|_{L^2(\Z_N)}^2 \geq \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_K}) \E(f|\B_K) \|_{L^2(\Z_N)}^2 + 2^{-2^k + 1} \eps.\end{equation} To do this we exploit the hypothesis $\Vert F_{K+1} \Vert_{U^{k-1}} > \eps^{1/2^k}$, which was \eqref{non-terminate}. By Lemma ef{antiuniform} and the definition \eqref{FK1-def} we have \[ |\left\langle (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_K}) (f-\E(f|\B_K)), \D F_{K+1} ightangle| = |\langle F_{K+1}, \D F_{K+1} angle| = \| F_{K+1} \|_{U^{k-1}}^{2^{k-1}} \geq \eps^{1/2}. \] On the other hand, from the bounds \eqref{f-disc-ok}, \eqref{om-small} and \eqref{FJ-bound} we have  egin{eqnarray*} & &  ig|\left\langle ({ f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}} - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K}}) (f-\E(f|\B_K)), \D F_{K+1} ightangle  ig|  \ & & \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad \leq  \Vert \D F_{K+1} \Vert_{\infty} \E  ig(({ f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}} - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K}}) |f - \E(f | \B_K)| ig) \ &  & \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad = O_{K,\eps}(1) \E  ig(({ f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}} - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K}}) (
u + 1) ig) \; = \; O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}),\end{eqnarray*} while from \eqref{trivial} and  \eqref{fbk-bound} we have  egin{eqnarray*} & &  ig|\left\langle (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) (f-\E(f|\B_K)), \D F_{K+1} - \E(\D F_{K+1}|\B_{K+1}) ightangle ig| \ & & \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad \leq  \Vert \D F_{K+1} - \E(\D F_{K+1} | \B_{K+1}) \Vert_{\infty} \E  ig((1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}})|f - \E(f | \B_K)| ig) \ & & \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad \leq  O(\eps) \E ig((1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}})(
u + 1) ig) \; = \; O(\epsilon). \end{eqnarray*} By the triangle inequality we thus have $$ |\left\langle (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) (f-\E(f|\B_K)), \E(\D F_{K+1}|\B_{K+1}) ightangle| \geq \eps^{1/2} - O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}) - O(\eps). $$ But since $(1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}})$, $\E(\D F_{K+1}|\B_{K+1})$, and $\E(f|\B_K)$ are all measurable in $\B_{K+1}$, we can replace $f$ by $\E(f|\B_{K+1})$, and so $$ |\left\langle (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) (\E(f|\B_{K+1})-\E(f|\B_K)), \E(\D F_{K+1}|\B_{K+1}) ightangle| \geq \eps^{1/2} - O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}) - O(\eps). $$ By the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and \eqref{FJ-bound} we obtain  egin{equation} \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) (\E(f|\B_{K+1}) - \E(f|\B_K)) \|_{L^2(\Z_N)} \geq 2^{-2^{k-1}+1} \eps^{1/2} - O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}) - O(\eps). \end{equation} Morally speaking, this implies \eqref{fj-increment} thanks to Pythagoras's theorem, but the presence of the exceptional sets $\Omega_K$ and $\Omega_{K+1}$ means that we have to exercise caution, especially since we have no $L^2$ control on $
u$. Recalling that $\E(f | \B_K) \leq 1 + O_{\eps,K}(\eta^{1/2})$ outside $\Omega_K$ (cf. \eqref{fbk-bound}), we observe that if $\eta < \eta_0(\eps, K)$ is sufficiently small then \[ \| ({ f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}} - { f 1}_{\Omega_K}) \E(f|\B_K) \|_{L^2(\Z_N)}^2 \leq 2 \Vert { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}} - { f 1}_{\Omega_K} \Vert_2^2 \leq 2 \Vert { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}} - { f 1}_{\Omega_K} \Vert_1 \leq 2\E { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}},\] which, by \eqref{om-small}, is $O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2})$. By the triangle inequality (and \eqref{fbk-bound}) we thus see that to prove \eqref{fj-increment} it will suffice to prove that \[ \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) \E(f|\B_{K+1}) \|_{L^2(\Z_N)}^2 \geq \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) \E(f|\B_K) \|_{L^2(\Z_N)}^2 + 2^{-2^k + 2} \eps - O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}) - O(\eps^{3/2}),\] since we can absorb the error terms $- O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}) - O(\eps^{3/2})$ into the $2^{-2^k + 2} \eps$ term by choosing $\eps$ sufficiently small depending on $k$, and $\eta$ sufficiently small depending on $K,\eps$. We write the left-hand side as $$ \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) \E(f|\B_K) + (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) (\E(f|\B_{K+1}) - \E(f|\B_K) \|_{L^2(\Z_N)}^2$$ which can be expanded using the cosine rule as  egin{align*} \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) \E(f|\B_K) \|_{L^2(\Z_N)}^2 &+ \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) (\E(f|\B_{K+1}) - \E(f|\B_K)) \|_{L^2(\Z_N)}^2 \ &+ 2 \left\langle (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) \E(f|\B_K), (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) (\E(f|\B_{K+1}) - \E(f|\B_K)) ightangle. \end{align*} Therefore by \eqref{pythagoras-targ} it will suffice to show the approximate orthogonality relationship $$ \left\langle (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) \E(f|\B_K), (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) (\E(f|\B_{K+1}) - \E(f|\B_K)) ightangle = O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}). $$ Since $(1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}})^2 = (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}})$, this can be rewritten as \[ \left\langle (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) \E(f|\B_K), \E(f|\B_{K+1}) - \E(f|\B_K) ightangle.\] Now note that $(1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_K}) \E(f|\B_K)$ is measurable with respect to $\B_K$, and hence orthogonal to $\E(f|\B_{K+1}) - \E(f|\B_K)$, since $\B_K$ is a sub-$\sigma$-algebra of $\B_{K+1}$.  Thus the above expression can be rewritten as $$ \left\langle ({ f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}} - { f 1}_{\Omega_K}) \E(f|\B_K), \E(f|\B_{K+1}) - \E(f|\B_K) ightangle.$$ Again, since the left-hand side is measurable with respect to $\B_{K+1}$, we can rewrite this as $$ \langle ({ f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}} - { f 1}_{\Omega_K}) \E(f|\B_K), f - \E(f|\B_K) angle.$$ Since $\E (f | \B_K)(x) \leq 2$ if $\eta < \eta_0(\eps, K)$ is sufficiently small and $x 
otin \Omega_K$ (cf. \eqref{fbk-bound}), we may majorise this by $$ 2\E  ig( ({ f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}} - { f 1}_{\Omega_K}) |f - \E(f|\B_K)|  ig).$$  Since we are working on the assumption that $0 \leq f(x) \leq 
u(x)$, we can bound this in turn by $$ 2\E ig( ({ f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}} - { f 1}_{\Omega_K}) (
u + \E(
u|\B_K))  ig).$$ Since $\E(
u | \B_K)(x) \leq 2$ for $x 
otin \Omega_K$ (cf. \eqref{uniform-dist}) this is no more than $$ 4\E ig( ({ f 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}} - { f 1}_{\Omega_K}) (
u + 1)  ig),$$ which is $O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2})$ as desired by \eqref{om-small}.  This concludes the proof of Proposition ef{relative}, and hence Theorem ef{main}.
nodes.section: A Furstenberg tower, and the proof of Theorem \ref{main}

nodes.name: Prove boundedness estimates (fbk-bound, f-disc-ok-2)
nodes.statement:
We begin by proving the bounds \eqref{fbk-bound}, \eqref{f-disc-ok-2}.  From \eqref{uniform-dist} we have $$ \| (1 - { f 1}_{\Omega_{K}}) \E( 
u | \B_{K} )\|_{L^\infty} \leq 1 + O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2});$$ since $f$ is non-negative and bounded pointwise by $
u$, we obtain \eqref{fbk-bound}.  The bound \eqref{f-disc-ok-2} then follows from \eqref{fbk-bound} and \eqref{FK1-def}, where we again use that $f$ is non-negative and bounded pointwise by $
u$.

nodes.name: Locate exceptional set via Proposition bohr-sigma
nodes.statement: We now apply Proposition \ref{bohr-sigma} (absorbing the multiplicative errors of $1+O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2})$) to conclude that we may find a set $\Omega$ in $\B_{K+1}$ such that $$ \E( (\nu + 1) {\bf 1}_{\Omega} ) = O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2})$$ and $$ \| (1 - {\bf 1}_{\Omega}) \E(\nu - 1 | \B_{K+1}) \|_{L^\infty} = O_{K,\eps}(\eta^{1/2}).$$ If we then set $\Omega_{K+1} := \Omega_K \cup \Omega$, then we can verify \eqref{om-small-2} and \eqref{uniform-dist-2} from \eqref{om-small} and \eqref{uniform-dist}.

nodes.name: Verify energy increment property
nodes.statement: It remains to verify \eqref{fj-increment}, the energy increment property, that is to say the statement \begin{equation} \| (1 - {\bf 1}_{\Omega_{K+1}}) \E(f|\B_{K+1}) \|_{L^2(\Z_N)}^2 \geq \| (1 - {\bf 1}_{\Omega_K}) \E(f|\B_K) \|_{L^2(\Z_N)}^2 + 2^{-2^k + 1} \eps.\end{equation} To do this we exploit the hypothesis $\Vert F_{K+1} \Vert_{U^{k-1}} > \eps^{1/2^k}$, which was \eqref{non-terminate}. By Lemma \ref{antiuniform} and the definition \eqref{FK1-def} we have \[ |\left\langle (1 - {\bf 1}_{\Omega_K}) (f-\E(f|\B_K)), \D F_{K+1} \right\rangle| = |\langle F_{K+1}, \D F_{K+1} \rangle| = \| F_{K+1} \|_{U^{k-1}}^{2^{k-1}} \geq \eps^{1/2}. \]

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{mainthm} assuming Proposition \ref{prime-majorant}
nodes.statement: Let $N$ be a large prime number.  Define the function $f \in L^1(\Z_N)$ by setting $f(n) := k^{-1}2^{-k-5}\tilde{\Lambda}(n)$ for $\epsilon_k N \leq n \leq 2\epsilon_k N$ and $f(n) = 0$ otherwise. From Dirichlet's theorem we observe that $$ \E(f) = \frac{k^{-1}2^{-k-5}}{N} \sum_{\epsilon_k N \leq n \leq 2 \epsilon_k N} \tilde \Lambda(n) = k^{-1}2^{-k-5} \epsilon_k (1 + o(1)).$$ We now apply Proposition \ref{prime-majorant} and Theorem \ref{main} to conclude that $$\mathbb{E} \big( f(x)f(x+r) \dots f(x + (k-1)r) \; \big| \; x,r \in \mathbb{Z}_N\big) \geq c(k,k^{-1}2^{-k-5} \epsilon_k) - o(1).$$ Observe that the degenerate case $r=0$ can only contribute at most $O(\frac{1}{N} \log^k N) = o(1)$ to the left-hand side and can thus be discarded. Furthermore, every progression counted by the expression on the left is not just a progression in $\mathbb{Z}_N$, but a genuine arithmetic progression of integers since $\epsilon_k < 1/k$.  Since the right-hand side is positive (and bounded away from zero) for sufficiently large $N$, the claim follows from the definition of $f$ and $\tilde \Lambda$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP43.7
nodes.statement: The first claim is trivial. The second claim is also trivial unless $Wn+1$ is prime.  From definition of $R$, we see that $Wn+1 > R$ if $N$ is sufficiently large. Then the sum over $d | Wn + 1$, $d \leq R$ in \eqref{truncated-divisor-sum} in fact consists of just the one term $d = 1$. Therefore $\Lambda_R(Wn + 1) = \log R$, which means that $\nu(n) = \frac{\phi(W)}{W}\log R \geq k^{-1}2^{-k-5} \widetilde{\Lambda}(n)$ by construction of $R$ and $N$ (assuming $\w(N)$ sufficiently slowly growing in $N$).

nodes.name: First claim ($\nu \geq 0$)
nodes.statement: The first claim is trivial.

nodes.name: Second claim (majorisation)
nodes.statement: The second claim is also trivial unless $Wn+1$ is prime.  From definition of $R$, we see that $Wn+1 > R$ if $N$ is sufficiently large. Then the sum over $d | Wn + 1$, $d \leq R$ in \eqref{truncated-divisor-sum} in fact consists of just the one term $d = 1$. Therefore $\Lambda_R(Wn + 1) = \log R$, which means that $\nu(n) = \frac{\phi(W)}{W}\log R \geq k^{-1}2^{-k-5} \widetilde{\Lambda}(n)$ by construction of $R$ and $N$ (assuming $\w(N)$ sufficiently slowly growing in $N$).

nodes.name: Proof of LP43.8
nodes.statement: Apply Proposition \ref{GY} with $m := t := 1$, $\psi_1(x_1) := x_1$ and $B := [\epsilon_k N, 2\epsilon_k N]$ (taking $N$ sufficiently large depending on $k$, of course). Comparing with Definition \ref{mu-def} we thus have \[ \E (\nu(x) \; | \; x \in [\epsilon_k N, 2\epsilon_k N]) = 1 + o(1).\] But from the same definition we clearly have \[ \E (\nu(x) \; | \; x \in \Z_N \backslash [\epsilon_k N, 2\epsilon_k N] ) = 1;\] Combining these two results confirms the lemma.

nodes.name: Proof of LP43.9
nodes.statement: We observe that $$ \prod_{p|\Delta} (1 + O_m(p^{-1/2})) \leq \prod_{1 \leq i < j \leq m} \bigg(\prod_{p|h_i-h_j} (1 + p^{-1/2}) \bigg)^{O_m(1)}.$$ By the arithmetic mean-geometric mean inequality (absorbing all constants into the $O_m(1)$ factor) we can thus take $\tau_m(n) := O_m(1) \prod_{p | n} (1 + p^{-1/2})^{O_m(1)}$ for all $n \neq 0$.  (The value of $\tau$ at 0 is irrelevant for this lemma since we are taking all the $h_i$ to be distinct). To prove the claim, it thus suffices to show that $$ \E\bigg( \prod_{p|n} (1 + p^{-1/2})^{O_m(q)} \; \bigg| \; 0 < |n| \leq N \bigg) = O_{m,q}(1) \hbox{ for all } 0 < q < \infty.$$ Since $(1 + p^{-1/2})^{O_m(q)}$ is bounded by $1 + p^{-1/4}$ for all but $O_{m,q}(1)$ many primes $p$, we have $$ \E\bigg( \prod_{p|n} (1 + p^{-1/2})^{O_m(q)} \;  \bigg| \; 0 < |n| \leq N \bigg) \leq O_{m,q}(1) \E\bigg( \prod_{p|n} (1 + p^{-1/4}) \; \bigg| \; 0 < n \leq N \bigg).$$ But $\prod_{p|n} (1 + p^{-1/4}) \leq \sum_{d|n} d^{-1/4}$, and hence \begin{eqnarray*} \E\bigg( \prod_{p|n} (1 + p^{-1/2})^{O_m(q)} \; \bigg| \; 0 < |n| \leq N \bigg) & \leq  & O_{m,q}(1) \frac{1}{2N} \sum_{1 \leq |n| \leq N} \sum_{d|n} d^{-1/4} \\ & \leq & O_{m,q}(1) \frac{1}{2N} \sum_{d=1}^N \frac{N}{d} d^{-1/4},\end{eqnarray*} which is $O_{m,q}(1)$ as desired.
